nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is propermutable in $G$ when there is a subgroup $B$ of $G$ with $G = N_G(H)B$ (every element of $G$ is a product $nb$ with $n$ in the normalizer $N_G(H)$ of $H$ and $b \in B$) such that $H$ permutes with every subgroup $X$ of $B$, that is, $HX = XH$.
nodes.title: Propermutable subgroups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is $2$-nilpotent when it has a normal subgroup $N$ of finite odd order whose index in $G$ is $2^k$ for some natural number $k$.
nodes.title: 2-nilpotent groups

nodes.summary: Let $H$ and $X$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H$ permutes with $X$ when $HX = XH$ as subsets of $G$, where $HX = \{hx : h \in H, x \in X\}$ and $XH = \{xh : x \in X, h \in H\}$.
nodes.title: Permuting subgroups

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(a).
nodes.title: Propermutability is not inherited by intermediate subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (A. N. Skiba): there exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (statement)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(b).
nodes.title: Propermutable subgroups of a non-abelian Sylow 2-subgroup force 2-nilpotency

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (A. N. Skiba), with the range $1 \le k < n$: let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (statement)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
